Results.ReviewText:
I had to buy a grill to serve as my main cooking device while renovating our cabin (it was gutted & had no kitchen the entire summer).  This little guy blew my mind.  I had a Silver Genesis for 13 years before buying my new Genesis so I knew I was buying a Weber.  This grill has been a lifesaver.  I literally do all my cooking on it.  Breakfast on the griddle and all the normal grilling tasks on the grates.  I had NO expectations that this thing would do a good job but it really has.  On my big Webers I could control the temperature and cook indirectly because of the size so I figured with this being small I wouldn't be able to control things as well.  Boy was I wrong.  Car camping feels like cheating it cooks so well.  Cleaning it is quick and easy because you simply lift the grates and wipe it out, the drip pan helps a lot too because I cook a lot of chicken thighs which produce a lot of fat which runs right into the removable drip pan.  Lastly, this think is so portable I find myself taking it everywhere.  I can easily get through a week of camping with a couple little fuel bottles which means I don't have to lug a huge propane tank and trip over the hose all day.
Just get it, you'll have it forever and each time you use it you will find something else you'll like about it.

I bought a 2200 about 10 years ago, and it's still going strong.  Since our guests asked for grills at the 3 cabins we have, we bought a 1200 (in a matching color) for each.  Not only do these things come together in a heartbeat, the right accessories ensure you'll be cooking for a long time.  I added 20 gallon propane tanks and line converters to each, along with a half griddle grate and covers and a collapsible stand.  Now our guests can cook breakfast, lunch and dinner on the grills.
The best parts of these grills are they work well, heat quickly, retain that heat while not taking a lot of fuel, are easy to clean and maintain, and last a long time.  A great investment, an easy way to cook, and these products look great over time.

Results.ReviewText: I’m a big Weber guy. I love all their products, so my review might be a little bias, but I’ll try not to. I still have a Smokey Joe, that I previously used for tailgating and parks. More and more places do not allow charcoal grills, so Weber Q at the local Home Depot was the obvious choice. I bought mine on sale along with the cart, cover and conversion propane hose for big tanks. I am impressed with how fast the grill heats up. Burgers and hot dogs grilled in no time. Flare ups, non-existent. I used to dis-like the grates, until I noticed they’re designed in a way that prevents burners from getting dirty. Still able to have awesome sear marks on chicken. Love the side tables, but hate waiting for the grates to cool to fold back into place. Cart is perfect, very(one hand) mobile, fits in the trunk of my wife’s two door Nissan, completely assembled. Love the cover, stays in place in windy weather. Haven’t used the big propane conversion line. Clean up is very easy. Don’t ignore the drip pan, it’ll build up quickly. Cart has two tool holders, wish Weber sold mini tools for smaller grills. If it’s like my other Webers, it’ll last forever. My Smokey Joe is 10+ years old. Replaced the grates once, that’s it. Back to Q, it’s awesome, who am I kidding. Does exactly what I need it to do. Take it with you, or use it at home. I’ve started using it for quick grills at home vs using the big grills. My son is crying, so I have to cut it short. Love it, buy it, if you need it. If you don’t, buy it any way because it’s great for a small family.
